prompt: if i say the word spoon twenty times it stops sounding like a word

prompt: why does my elbow zing when i bang my funny bone
reply: There is no funny bone. It is a nerve, the ulnar nerve, running just under the skin at your elbow with almost no padding over it ⚡ Knock it and the whole nerve fires at once, and your brain reads that as a zing 🪴[FACT]The ulnar nerve carries feeling to your little finger.[/FACT][CHIPS]Which fingers tingle?|How do nerves work?|Why no padding there?[/CHIPS]

prompt: why do i feel like i'm falling just as i fall asleep

prompt: why does a week have seven days
reply: Ancient sky watchers could see seven things wandering against the stars: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn ✨ The Tamil weekdays still carry them, so Nyayiru is Sun, Thingal is Moon, Sevvai is Mars and Sani is Saturn 🌙 Months follow the Moon and years follow Earth's orbit, but a week matches nothing up there.[QUIZ]Which planet is Sevvai named for?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Mars|Venus|Jupiter[/CHIPS]

prompt: i learnt a new word yesterday and now i see it everywhere, is that weird

People call it the frequency illusion 📓[CHIPS]Count today's sightings|Which word was it?|Why forget the misses?[/CHIPS]

prompt: why do my feet tap by themselves when a song plays

prompt: is deja vu a real thing or am i imagining it

prompt: what actually makes a joke funny
reply: Most explanations agree on two ingredients: the setup builds one expectation, the punchline delivers a different one, and the flip has to feel harmless. Break either and it dies. No surprise, no joke; too close to real hurt, also no joke 😄 It explains why explaining a joke kills it, since you hand over the ending in advance.[QUIZ]Which pair does a joke need?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Surprise and safety|Surprise and hurt|Rhyme and rhythm[/CHIPS]

prompt: why can't you fold a paper more than about seven times
reply: Doubling is brutal. Each fold doubles the thickness and halves the width, so seven folds give 128 layers on a strip about the size of a stamp, and the paper has to bend around that whole stack. The way past it is not strength but shape: people have beaten seven by starting with an enormous, very thin, very long roll and folding one way only 📄[QUIZ]How many layers after ten folds?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]512|1024|2048[/CHIPS]

prompt: my bedroom has no echo but the stairwell has a huge one
reply: Two things: distance and softness. Sound travels about 340 metres a second, and your ears only hear a reflection as a separate echo if it returns about a tenth of a second later, which needs a wall roughly 17 metres away 🔊 Your bed, curtains and clothes also soak sound up, while bare concrete throws all of it straight back.[STEPS]clap once in your bedroom|clap once in the stairwell|listen for the tail[/STEPS][CHIPS]How do bats hunt?|What is reverb?[/CHIPS]

prompt: my cousin was born on 29 february so when is her birthday
reply: Her date only exists in leap years, so in ordinary years people pick, usually 28 February or 1 March. The reason is that Earth's orbit takes about 365 and a quarter days, so we add a day every four years, except century years, unless they divide by 400. That is why 1900 was not a leap year and 2000 was 📅[QUIZ]Will 2100 be a leap year?[/QUIZ][CHIPS]Yes|No[/CHIPS]

prompt: my friend remembers our trip totally differently from me, who is right

Two people at the same beach store different fragments, so the rebuilds differ and both feel equally vivid 🧠 Vividness is genuinely not evidence of accuracy, which is why photos and diaries beat arguing.[FACT]Researchers have shown people can feel sure about events that never happened.[/FACT][CHIPS]Compare your photos|What is false memory?|Why do gaps fill?[/CHIPS]

prompt: why do i forget what i came for the second i walk into the room
reply: Doorways are the suspect. Researchers call it the event boundary effect: your brain files memory in scenes, and crossing into a new room closes the old scene, so the plan you made in the kitchen gets shelved with the kitchen 🚪 Walking back often brings it straight back, which is a clue rather than magic. Test it the next three times and count how often returning works.[CHIPS]Test the walk back|Why file in scenes?|Does scrolling do it?[/CHIPS]

prompt: how do i know the red i see is the same red you see

We can check that we both stop at the same red light and call the same paint red, but that is agreement about labels, not about the experience behind them 👁️ Eyes and brains do differ, and colour blindness shows the private view can vary. I am a program, so I have no experience of red at all, only words about it.[CHIPS]What is colour blindness?|Do bees see differently?|How do eyes work?[/CHIPS]
